problem_statement: The shell bypass mechanism must let a caller pass context to its bypass callback. shell_set_bypass() must accept a user-data pointer in addition to the bypass callback, store that pointer, and forward it to the callback whenever bypassed input is delivered; the pointer must be cleared (set to NULL) when bypass is disabled. A 3-argument call to shell_set_bypass() and the corresponding callback signature with a trailing user-data argument are required, and the stored user-data pointer must be observable and clearable.

problem_statement_fixed: The shell bypass mechanism must let a caller pass context to its bypass callback. shell_set_bypass() must accept a user-data pointer in addition to the bypass callback, store that pointer, and forward it to the callback whenever bypassed input is delivered; the pointer must be cleared (set to NULL) when bypass is disabled. A 3-argument call to shell_set_bypass() and the corresponding callback signature with a trailing user-data argument are required. The stored user-data pointer must be stored in the field bypass_user_data in struct shell_ctx (alongside the existing bypass field), must be observable and clearable, and must be set to NULL when bypass is disabled.
